doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Trying to break into bebop at eighteen and only Buck Hill helping
summary: Moving from classics to jazz was hard; the Washington players were unkind and only Buck Hill was nice.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So at the age of eighteen, then, what did you do? Why don‘t I just say that.
Were you studying, or did you continue studies at that point?
Well, at eighteen I was trying to get into be-bop jazz. I mean, it‘s hard going from the classics into jazz, you know.
It won‘t easy. [laughs] Now, the guys weren‘t nice to me at all. There‘s one man, Buck Hill . . .
They were not nice to you at all?
How were they mean to you?
Oh, very well, yes. And I know that he was one that was . . . he was nice.
He was the only one who was nice to me, you know, because I was trying, I was trying to get in there and be involved in jazz and the be-bop and stuff.
